description: GEOTHERMOS is MATLAB software that assesses the geothermal potential of an area by combining geological, thermal and engineering parameters in a physics-based workflow. It was developed within the Italian research community by the National Research Council (CNR), the University of Padova and the University of Trieste, with Gianluca Gola, Adele Manzella, Antonio Galgaro and Magdala Tesauro as authors, and published on Zenodo in February 2026 as part of the InGEO project funded under Italy's PRIN 2022 PNRR programme. It supports site screening and resource evaluation for medium- and high-temperature geothermal systems, estimating both how much heat can be extracted and how efficiently it can be produced. The workflow has four steps: subsurface evaluation of temperature and petrophysical parameters; a production borehole model coupled with the reservoir; thermodynamic simulation of a chosen power plant cycle; and an economic analysis of the levelised cost of energy to judge feasibility. Coverage is not tied to a place. The software is downloadable from Zenodo as a RAR archive under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: MATLAB is required, and no source repository, documentation or validation cases were found beyond the Zenodo record. Simulation uses are screening geothermal power and heat projects for capacity planning. Related records: model-gengeo also estimates geothermal plant performance and costs.
